column1: # FS114-YB stage 2: the instance file's statements (as the owner quoted them) against FS114-Y's record

column3: it is a valid fragment, and it holds the closed disc B̄(P_j, R) about every midline four-colour vertex P_j for every R with R² < (7 + 3√5)/4; no valid extension of the strip holds that disc at R ≥ φ²/√2 (the disc would then hold the stop point Q)

B_k's two close complementary partners Z^R_k, Z^L_{k+1} meet ω(B_k) at four distinct points A_k, C_k, A_{k+1}, D_{k+1}, so no valid map agrees with the disk near B_k, Z^R_k, Z^L_{k+1}, and no third unit-arc boundary at B_k, nor any choice of arcs, repairs it; and A_k + A_{k+1} − B_k is the central corner A_{k+3}

the blue and orange routes to a fourth colour at C_0 fail with the rest of the disk unchanged: the only blue tile straddling ω(C_0 + e(72°)/100) is T2_0, the only orange one T1_0, and at named points of T2_0 ∩ B(C_0, 1) and T1_0 ∩ B(C_0, 1) the free set, with the cut tile ignored, is exactly the tile's own colour

In the strip's geometry the six tiles at a valley V_m (the arches U_{m−1}, U_m and the top tile T_m) and at the apex of U_{m+1} (U_{m+1}, T_{m+1}, T_{m+2}) pairwise straddle distance 1, so the two vertices are complementary under every colouring; V_m's three boundary curves lie on ω(P_{m−1}), ω(P_{m+1}) and a segment, none on ω(Q_m); so, by FS112-N3-COR3, no valid map contains these six tiles
Every valid colouring of the strip's geometry is [AxenovichEtAl2014]'s, up to a permutation of the six colours

Every valid colouring of the disk's geometry is the printed one up to a permutation (its central tile and five ring-1 tiles pairwise straddle distance 1); so PENT holds under every colouring, and no valid map contains the disk's geometry near any B_k
In a valid map, any two close complementary cubic trichromatic partners u′, u″ of a cubic trichromatic vertex u share a common unit point with u: (ω(u) ∩ ω(u′)) ∩ (ω(u) ∩ ω(u″)) ≠ ∅

If two cubic vertices u, u′ at distance < 2 have six incident tiles that pairwise straddle distance 1, they are complementary under every colouring, and each common unit point of ω(u) and ω(u′) must be a leaving centre of both
